hold` is refused: hosted grading is suite-wide. A\ndisabled case with the same override is ignored, matching how repetitions\nare
checked. Authored\n`defaults.toolPolicy` and non-empty `defaults.validity` gates are refused at\nhosted CLI launch (`TOOL_POLICY_U
NSUPPORTED` / the corresponding validity\nrefusal). Hosted platform-authored suites do not currently have a backend\ntool-policy f
ield or enforcement path, so the CLI does not upload a suite that\nwould claim those guarantees. When supported by an eval runner,
`toolPolicy`\nis enforced at execution time with denied tools kept visible but blocked;\nserver annotations are advisory and **UN

r case and is not uploaded as a suite `minIterations` floor.\nAuthored `defaults.systemPrompt` and `defaults.temperature` are uplo
aded as\nexecution defaults; omitted fields stay omitted so the platform applies its\nown defaults. `target.hosts` and `target.env
ironment` are attached before\nlaunch. A file environment takes precedence over file hosts for that launch,\nwhile an explicit CLI
target takes precedence over both. When an explicit CLI\ntarget is provided (for example `--host`), the file's `target.hosts` are
\n**not** synchronized to the suite's persisted host attachments — the suite\nkeeps whatever hosts it already has. Host attachment
synchronization only\nruns when no explicit CLI target overrides the file. Environment attachment\nsynchronization is unaffected

and always runs.

Without `--idempotency-key`, the CLI mints a fresh UUID for every invocation
and prints it to stderr before l
aunch (`Eval idempotency key: <key>`). Each\ninvocation therefore starts and bills a new run. To retry a launch whose\nresponse wa
s lost — without starting a second run — pass the key that was\nprinted: `--idempotency-key <printed-key>`. A replay is marked `de

duped` in
the receipt and human output. `--notes` is not part of the key.

##### Imported cases: live tool resolution, and per-

run approval

Every file run performs the same live check `eval validate --project` performs,
**before it writes anything**. It
is not opt-in and there is no flag to skip\nit. A file with no deterministic `toolCall` steps asks no question and pays no\nround

trip.

What happens when a deterministic reference does not resolve depends on the
case:

| Case | Outcome |
| - | - |
| S
elected (enabled, and named by `--case` if you used it) | The launch **refuses before the suite is synced** — nothing is written a
nd nothing is billed |\n| Imported, not selected | Its claim is rewritten to `unresolved` (keeping `sourceCaseKey`) and it is **st
ill persisted**, so the hosted record says what MCPJam found rather than still asserting a claim about a missing tool |\n| Native,
not selected | Left exactly as authored. A hand-written case never acquires an `import` block from this — \"somebody wrote this\"
and \"something converted this\" are different facts |\n\nEach target is checked on **its own** server set. `--host` is checked a
gainst\nthat host's configured servers rather than the file's, because that is the set\nthe run connects — validating `target.serv
ers` would approve a tool the host\ncannot reach. A host the FILE declares uses its own `servers` list when it\ndeclares one (thos
e are attached to the host before launch) and the host's\nconfigured set when the field is omitted. An explicitly empty `servers:
[]`\nis a real, empty set — it clears the attachment before launch — and is\nvalidated as such, never as an omitted field. A step
not be enumerated before the suite exists\n(`--all-targets`, `--compose-*`), or a host does not report a server set, or a\nhost pi

ns a server the project no longer has, the launch refuses rather than
assuming the references are fine.

`--case` accepts a hos
ted row id, which does not exist yet when this check\nruns. A selector this stage cannot map is therefore treated as possibly nami

ng
any enabled case, so an unresolved reference still refuses; the launcher
resolves the selector itself a moment later.

A se

lected `approximated` case refuses unless this invocation approves it:

| Flag | Required | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `--a
llow-approximated <case...>` | No | Approve an `approximated` imported case for **this run only**, by AUTHORED case id (`cases[].i
d`). Repeatable. `--file` runs only |\n| `--approval-reason <text>` | With the above | Why the approximations are acceptable for t
his run. 1–500 characters after trimming; one reason covers every approval in the invocation |\n\n```bash theme={\"theme\":\"css-v
ariables\"}\nmcpjam cloud eval run --file .mcpjam/evals/s_billing.yaml \\\n --allow-approximated c_refund_partial \\\n --approva

l-reason "Reviewed against the upstream rubric; ENG-4821"
```

Checked before anything is billed, each with its own message:
approving a\n**native** case (nothing to approve), a **claimed-exact** one (needs no\napproval), an **unsupported** or **unresolve
d** one (approval covers a case\nwhose behaviour was approximated, not one whose behaviour is missing), a\n**disabled** or **unsel
ected** one (the run will not execute it), an unknown\nid, or the same id twice. The flags are refused outright with `--suite`: a\

nhosted suite's cases are not the ones this invocation authored, so an
authored-id selector has nothing to resolve against.

**
The approval belongs to the run, never to the case.** You supply an id and a\nreason and nothing else — the approver and the times
tamp are derived by the\nserver and frozen into that run's own snapshot, because a caller-supplied\napprover would file one person
's approval under another's name and a\ncaller-supplied timestamp could be backdated past the edit that invalidated the\nclaim. No

thing persists: edit the suite, re-sync, or launch again, and the flags
are required again.

Scheduled runs and GitHub-App runs
cannot approve anything. A scheduled suite\ncontaining a selected approximation is refused by platform policy, which is the\ninte

nded behaviour — an unattended job is exactly the caller that must not be
able to wave one through.

`--file` pointing at creat
e-API JSON (no `schemaVersion`) is a usage error\nthat names `eval create --file`. The converse is also true: `eval create --file`

on a versioned suite file names `eval run --file`.

Export of a file-owned suite writes `declaredId` as `suite.id`. Export of
a\nUI-owned suite derives a stable file identity (`s_export_<sourceSuiteId>`),\nso importing the exported file creates a file-owne

d clone rather than
re-claiming the original UI suite.

When the run targets an **attached project environment** (`eval environ

ments
set`), it executes against that environment's resolved host config, closed
| Flag | Required | Description |
| - | - | -
|\n| `--suite <id-or-name>` | Yes | Eval suite name or ID |\n| `--project <id-or-name>` | No | Project name or ID (defaults to the

most recently updated project) |

### `cloud eval validate`

Validate a local eval **suite file** — the versioned declarative
document that\ndescribes a suite, its defaults and its cases (`schemaVersion: \"1\"`, YAML\ncanonical, JSON accepted, conventiona

lly `.mcpjam/evals/*.yaml`).

Offline by default: without `--project` this command builds no API client, reads
no API key and n
ever touches the network. Passing `--project` is the only thing\nthat changes that, and it is keyed off the FLAG — a linked direct

ory or an
`MCPJAM_PROJECT` in the environment never turns the offline command into a
networked one.

| Flag | Required | Descr

iption |
| - | - | - |
| `--file <path>` | Yes | Suite file to validate, `.yaml` or `.json` (or `-` for stdin) |
| `--project <
id-or-name>` | No | Also resolve the file's deterministic tool references against this project's live servers. Opt-in; authenticat

es and makes network calls |

| Exit code | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `0` | Valid |
| `1` | Parsed, but invalid against the suite
-file contract. Every finding is reported, not just the first. `eval run --file` on the same bytes exits **2** — 1 is reserved the
